profiles.Failure modes: The filament must be dried in the device with exact thermoregulation (ideally laboratory dryer) – before drying the whole spool, put a little piece of filament into the device for the test of functionality. If the material becomes softer or loses its original shape, lower the drying temperature. In the case of loss of transparency, use a different device. The spool can’t be put into the environment without a controlled value of relative humidity after drying. The cooling process must be taken in the desiccator (or in the sealing box with the content of silica gel). If the hot spool is placed into an environment with higher humidity, the moisture may be absorbed back in about 10 minutes. And possibly on a higher level of moisture than it was before drying! The coil should not be left in the dryer after it has been switched off, as there is still evaporated moisture in the environment which can be absorbed back into the filament in the same way.

evidence.Finding: Thanks to its PTFE content, Fiberlogy PETG+PTFE enables the printing of sliding parts, guides, gears, and other components subjected to low or moderate loads , which are characterized by minimal friction and a longer service life. At the same time, the material retains all the advantages of PET-G: ease of printing, high adhesion to the build plate, chemical resistance, and good impact strength .

evidence.Finding: ASA+AF filament retains all the advantages of classic ASA while offering even greater resistance to wear and mechanical damage . The material has a reduced coefficient of friction, which ensures increased resistance to abrasion (tribological wear). Thanks to its resistance to UV radiation and weather conditions, the material is ideal for outdoor applications, such as automotive parts, drone components, device housings, or components exposed to impacts and fluctuating temperatures. The filament is heat-resistant up to 94°C.

evidence.Finding: Fiberlogy CPE ANTIBAC is a modern 3D printing filament that combines high mechanical and thermal strength with unique antibacterial properties. Thanks to the use of silver nanoparticles, the material effectively inhibits the growth of microorganisms on the surface of printed objects, as confirmed by microbiological tests. Fiberlogy CPE ANTIBAC demonstrated a complete (100%) reduction of E. coli and over a 92% reduction of Staphylococcus aureus in the initial test, and in repeat tests, its effectiveness remained at 100% and 97%, respectively.

No medical certification or guaranteed antibacterial service inferred.
